statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120139 (PostgreSQL tuple-size integer wraparound executes arbitrary code) in 16.16 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120139/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix is two commits on the REL_16_STABLE branch, both tagged Security: CVE-2026-120139 and Backpatch-through: 14: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/aa2d0aefec71eec88dbab334b42a5f83360c1df7 adds overflow-checked tuple-size arithmetic in src/backend/access/common/heaptuple.c, src/backend/access/heap/heaptoast.c, src/backend/executor/execTuples.c, src/backend/utils/adt/array_userfuncs.c, src/backend/utils/adt/multirangetypes.c and two headers, and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/c152f62ac61803d62fe315edeed573ff90ed6e8a hardens related allocations in src/backend/access/common/detoast.c, src/backend/access/common/toast_compression.c, src/backend/utils/adt/array_userfuncs.c, src/include/access/tableam.h and src/include/varatt.h; both commits are in the REL_16_16 release tag and not in REL_16_15. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 16.16-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.16 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 report 16.13, 16.14 and 16.15 and are affected. As a check, the 16.16-r0 server binary contains the error messages these commits add ("multirange is too big" and "toast object size is too big") on both architectures, and the server binaries of 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 do not. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120139 under its 16.16-r0 secfixes.

CVE-2026-120139 (PostgreSQL tuple-size integer wraparound executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.12: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120139/ and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. 17.12 is the fixed release listed for major version 17. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch is the upgrade to upstream 17.12 and lists CVE-2026-120139 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 17.12-r0 package for Alpine 3.23 is built from that APKBUILD and the upstream 17.12 source release, and its postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on both x86_64 and aarch64. Every earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0) is an earlier upstream release whose server binary reports that older version, so it is affected; 17.12-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120139, an integer wraparound in in-memory tuple-size calculations that lets a database user execute arbitrary code via oversized tuple data, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120139/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120139, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Earlier 17 releases are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
